_what: The vocabulary a look uses so a colour-adapting extension (Dark Reader, a forced-colours or high-contrast mode) cannot pull a surface and its words apart, as DATA. An extension decides from how a variable is USED whether it is a background or a text colour, so no variable plays both parts: a ground is only ever a background or a fill, words are only ever a text colour, a mark is only ever a line or a shape that carries no words. A surface that holds words is an HTML background (never an SVG fill, which an extension reads as a text colour), and its words are a words variable named for the ground they sit on. Each look declares every name below (src/themes/<look>/*.css); a part reads a name with the older variable as its fallback, so a look that has not yet declared one is drawn as before.
ink_for_words: A brand colour bright enough for a line may be too light for words or for a filled control with white words on it; a look names a deeper ink for those (the site's --thread-ink) and keeps the bright one for marks.
